text:
release-manager: Deploybot flagged a problem on rc-2026.03.21. SBOM mismatch for multi-arch image `inference-runtime:rc-2026-03-21` — arm64 layer missing provenance. Deploy is blocked. Need decision: pin, rollback, or staggered carveout?

deploybot: :warning: deploy halted for release rc-2026.03.21. Reason: SBOM provenance mismatch (arm64). Action required: human approval or artifact pin/rollback. See /deploy status 56fa.

eng-sre: Saw the same. The x86_64 manifest is clean, arm64 layer doesn't have cosign signature in the manifest. Could be a builder upload race or sign step skipped for arm.

security: Can you paste the exact SBOM diff? We need to see which layer metadata is missing. If it's just signature metadata we might accept a timeboxed exception but need audit trail.

qa-lead: Quick note — smoke tests passed on the staging x86_64 canary earlier. We haven't exercised arm64 in staging for this image.

release-manager: Proposal: staggered rollout — publish to x86_64 clusters today (contiguous regions), hold arm64 images until provenance is resolved. Option B: pin to previous digest for arm64 only and continue. Which gives us fastest safe ship?

security: Exception only if we get evidence (builder logs + cosign upload) within 4 hours and an audit ticket. Prefer pin for arm64 to previous digest (sha256:8b7f...) and continue x86_64.

legal: Need to confirm no new third-party license changes in the arm64 layer. If artifact changes include new libs, we can't ship without approval. Can someone run `sbom-compare` and post the license matrix snapshot?

devops: I can pin arm64 to previous digest. CI artifact store still has `sha256:8b7f...` for arm. Pinning command (k8s image override):
```
kubectl set image deploy/inference inference-runtime=inference-runtime@sha256:8b7f... -n prod
```
Or for Helm:
```
helm upgrade inference ./chart --set image.repository=inference-runtime --set image.digest=sha256:8b7f...
```
I can push a hotfix helm diff and roll out only to clusters flagged for arm64.

eng-sre: If we do pin for arm64, we should also enable a feature-flag to disable the new opt-in model routing on arm64 so we minimize surface area. product — can we toggle that?

product: Yes we can gate the new routing flag by arch via rollout config. That will preserve behavior for arm64 users while allowing x86 to get the new path.

infra-eng: I'll prepare a regional topology map to ensure x86-only rollout doesn't accidentally hit arm64-only edge pools. Need a quick list of clusters running arm64 workloads.

release-manager: OK plan A (preferred): 1) Pin arm64 to previous digest 2) Unblock deploy for x86_64 only 3) Gate new routing via feature flag for arm64 4) Timebox 4 hours for security/legal evidence, if provided we reconcile and push new arm64 image; otherwise we schedule a targeted replacement in the next maintenance window.

security: Works for me. Security will accept timeboxed exception pending logs + cosign attestations within 4 hours. Opening audit ticket now: AUDIT-2026-332.

legal: Please attach the `sbom-compare` output to AUDIT-2026-332. If license matrix unchanged we sign off.

devops: On it — creating helm diff + pin change, will run canary to x86 clusters only. Expected rollout start in ~12 minutes. I'll post the diff here.

devops: ```
--- a/values.yaml
+++ b/values.yaml
@@
-image:
-  repository: inference-runtime
-  tag: rc-2026-03-21
+image:
+  repository: inference-runtime
+  digest: sha256:8b7f...  # pin arm64 to previous safe build
```

qa-lead: Once canary is up on x86 clusters I'll run the smoke/regression subset. Tag me when done.

eng-sre: I'll monitor latency/error rates and KV cache behavior during the x86-only rollout. If anything spikes, we abort.

release-manager: I'll update the release notes to reflect the partial rollout and mitigation: "arm64 image held due to SBOM provenance; arm64 users remain on previous runtime; follow-up scheduled."

product: Noted — updating customer-facing notes to include "limited rollout" language and expected timeline.

devops: Canary started on x86 clusters. deploybot: observe ID 56fa. Posting rollout link: https://deploys.internal/r/56fa

deploybot: :white_check_mark: canary x86_64 rollout succeeded (50 hosts). No regressions observed in initial checks.

qa-lead: Smoke ok on canary. No obvious regressions.

eng-sre: Metrics stable so far (10m). Proceeding with phased x86 rollout.

legal: Received sbom-compare diff — no license changes. ACK on legal side. Attaching to AUDIT-2026-332.

security: Received builder logs and cosign upload timestamps — evidence looks fine for a previously uploaded artifact; however the arm manifest never propagated the cosign attestation. Security will track and request a rebuild pipeline fix. We consider artifact OK once attestation is present.

release-manager: Closing decision thread: proceed with x86 rollout, arm64 pinned, feature flag gated, 4-hour timebox for attestation. devops/infra — schedule a follow-up to unpin and redeploy once fixed.

devops: Follow-up ticket created: REL-FIX-2026-98 for pipeline attestation replay + redeploy window.

release-manager: Thanks everyone. :tada:
